key_insight: A privacy-preserving local pipeline combining a small language model with regular expressions can accurately extract uncoded UTI features from multilingual primary care EHR notes.
clinical_relevance: This approach helps turn free-text EHR narratives into structured data without sending sensitive records to cloud AI services, supporting safer secondary use of routine clinical documentation.
method: Ran Phi4-mini (3.8B) locally inside the institutional firewall via Ollama.
Refined prompts with clinicians and added post-processing regular expressions for six UTI features: fever, nitrites, leukocytes, lumbar pain, abdominal pain, and haematuria.
Validated against a double-blind clinician gold standard and an adversarial synthetic dataset with noisy multilingual notes.
evidence_signal: In clinician review, the pipeline achieved 93.8% accuracy, 83.6% sensitivity, 96.6% specificity, 87.1% PPV, and 95.5% NPV, with 15,498 narratives screened and 4,663 feature occurrences identified.
watch_item: Performance may drop outside the validated note style or language mix, so local deployment still needs site-specific testing and monitoring for edge cases.
paper_title: Uncoded Clinical Features from Multilingual Electronic Health Records in Catalonia: Development and Validation Study
